title: The Z(p) family under Schanuel
subtitle: A focused reading note from the Pirate Chest
author: Zolton / EncapsulatorP · with ChatGPT

blocks.text: Euler’s even-zeta formula gives exact rational coefficients cₚ for every odd integer p ≥ 3. Assuming complex Schanuel, π and any finite list of the corresponding Z(p) values are algebraically independent.

blocks.label: Conditional on complex Schanuel
blocks.text: The zeta reduction is unconditional. The independence conclusion in this argument assumes the full complex Schanuel conjecture. Distinct odd exponents and nonzero rational coefficients are part of the hypotheses.
First identify the exact Bernoulli coefficient. Then apply the conjecture to iπ and the selected real π-power exponents; field containment gives the required transcendence-degree bound.

blocks.label: Conditional proposition
blocks.text: Assume the full complex Schanuel conjecture. For pairwise distinct odd integers p₁, …, pₖ ≥ 3, the numbers π, Z(p₁), …, Z(pₖ) are algebraically independent over ℚ.

“Algebraically independent” means that no nonzero polynomial with rational coefficients in these k + 1 variables vanishes on the tuple. The next page gives the deduction and keeps the assumption visible.

The rational-coefficient reduction is unconditional. Algebraic independence of π and the selected Z(p) values, including the resulting individual-transcendence conclusions, follows under the stated complex Schanuel assumption.

blocks.label: Why the complex version matters
blocks.text: The selected inputs include iπ. A real-only version of Schanuel is not the assumption used in this proof.
The Euler counterexample has a domain

This refutes a blanket transcendence claim allowing every nonzero complex algebraic coefficient q. It does not refute a claim restricted to rational or real q, since i is neither. Lindemann’s algebraic-input theorem does not directly apply to cpπp, whose input is transcendental.
The deduction uses the stated conjecture, the even-zeta formula and the transcendence of π. Field containment provides the required bound.
